questions.question: The arithmetic mean of 25 observations is 32.6. If the arithmetic mean of the first 24 observations is 30, what is the 25th observation?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Deviation Method**: The 25th observation accounts for the total change in the mean.

Change in Mean = 32.6 − 30 = 2.6

Total Deviation = 24 × 2.6 = 62.4

25th observation = **New Mean** + **Total Deviation** = 32.6 + 62.4 = 95

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Arithmetic Mean of 25 **observations** = 32.6

Arithmetic Mean of the first 24 **observations** = 30

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = **Mean** × **Total Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e18964a26b748540a39f38cc7219cb6dcdd635d8c2660fb696ebeb940bd7c0d9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total sum** of 25 observations = 25 × 32.6 = 815

⇒ **Total sum** of first 24 observations = 24 × 30 = 720

⇒ 25th observation = **Total Sum (25)** − **Total Sum (24)**

⇒ 25th observation = 815 − 720 = 95

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Formula

The average or **Mean (x¯)** is calculated as the sum of all values divided by the total number of values: x¯ = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n.

Effect of Inclusion/Exclusion

When a new value is added, the **New Sum** = (Old Average × Old Count) + New Value. Conversely, New Value = (New Average × New Count) − (Old Average × Old Count).

Deviation Concept

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero (∑(xᵢ − x¯) = 0).

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper professes to sell his goods at a 35% loss but uses a false balance and gains 85%. The actual weight (rounded off to one decimal place) he uses for 1 kg is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Effective Multiplier** logic: Total Gain Factor = Price Factor × Weight Factor.

Total Gain 85% → Factor = 1.85 | Loss 35% → Factor = 0.65.

Weight Factor = 1000 / **Actual Weight** (x).

1.85 = 0.65 × (1000 / x) ⇒ x = 650 / 1.85.

x = 351.35... ≈ 351.4 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 351.4 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Professed Loss = 35%, **Overall Gain** = 85%, Standard weight = 1000 gm.

Let the **Actual Weight** used by the shopkeeper be x gm.

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 gm be ₹1.

⇒ **CP** of 1000 gm = ₹1000.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** at 35% loss = 1000 − (35% of 1000) = ₹650.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03f6134159e0888421f5f18356799918e50debb43c01893ba2f5bef1f5e6df67.png] 

⇒ The shopkeeper actually gives x gm for ₹650.

⇒ **Actual CP** of x gm = ₹x.

⇒ **Overall Gain%** = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ 85 = [(650 − x) / x] × 100

⇒ 0.85 = (650 / x) − 1

⇒ 1.85 = 650 / x

⇒ x = 650 / 1.85 = 351.351...

⇒ x ≈ 351.4 gm (rounded to one decimal place).

**∴ The correct answer is 351.4 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Formula

Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) / False Weight] × 100, assuming goods are sold at cost price.

Overall Profit with Price Change

Final Gain/Loss % = [((100 ± P/L%) / 100) × (True Weight / False Weight) − 1] × 100.

Multiplier Method

Effective Multiplier (Mₜₒₜₐₗ) = Mₚᵣᵢ꜀ₑ × Mwₑᵢgₕₜ. If M > 1, it is a profit; if M < 1, it is a loss.

questions.question: Add (11)/(16) and 0.4375. What is the sum in decimal form?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the **fraction 11/16** into its **decimal equivalent**: 11 ÷ 16 = **0.6875**.

Perform the **addition** with the given **decimal**: 0.6875 + 0.4375 = **1.125**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction = **11/16**

Decimal = **0.4375**

**Formula Used:**

Decimal to Fraction conversion: **Value / 10ⁿ** (where n is the number of decimal places).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4750d0e32e7adf6ae365e173a164154aa553e90c57f2ba2f6bf14a82c45959c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert 0.4375 to a **fraction**: 0.4375 = 4375 ÷ 10000

⇒ Simplify the **fraction**: 4375/10000 = 875/2000 = 175/400 = 35/80 = **7/16**

⇒ Calculate the **Sum**: 11/16 + 7/16 = (11 + 7) ÷ 16

⇒ **Sum** = 18/16 = 9/8

⇒ Convert **9/8** to **decimal form**: 9 ÷ 8 = **1.125**

**∴ The correct answer is 1.125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fraction to Decimal Conversion

A **fraction** is converted to a **decimal** by dividing the numerator by the denominator. If the denominator is in the form 2m × 5ⁿ, the **decimal** will be **terminating**.

Adding Decimals

To add **decimals**, align the **decimal points** and add as whole numbers, then place the **decimal point** directly below the others in the sum.

Like Fractions

Fractions with the **same denominator** are called **like fractions**. Their **addition** or subtraction is done by performing the operation on the numerators while keeping the denominator constant.

questions.question: A sum of ₹2000 is invested at 20% compound interest per annum, compounded annually for 2 years. What is the compound interest earned at the end of 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** for 2 years = x + y + (xy/100)%

⇒ 20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44%

**Compound Interest** (CI) = 44% of **₹2000**

⇒ 0.44 × 2000 = ₹880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Principal (P)** = ₹2000, **Rate (R)** = 20%, **Time (n)** = 2 years

Formula Used: **Amount (A)** = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cedb265cb4b25d2549d91db70e8a2bdf3e5457dc2049a9db147f0f89d3f90a4b.png] 

⇒ A = 2000(1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A = 2000(1.2)²

⇒ A = 2000 × 1.44 = ₹2880

⇒ **Compound Interest** = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 2880 − 2000 = ₹880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference (D) between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is given by D = P × (R/100)².

Effective Rate Formula

To find the equivalent single percentage for two successive increases of x% and y%, use the formula: x + y + (xy/100)%.

Compound Interest Ratio Method

For 2 years, the ratio 2:1 can be used. CI = 2 × (Interest on P) + 1 × (Interest on Interest).

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 55%, 35% and 45% in three successive months, but increases by 40% in the fourth month. What is the percentage decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Round off to 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Multiplier Method** to find the final price ratio.

Final Price Factor = 0.45 × 0.65 × 0.55 × 1.4 = 0.225225

Net Percentage Decrease = (1 − 0.225225) × 100 = 77.4775%

Rounding to 2 decimal places, we get 77.48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Successive decreases of 55%, 35%, 45% and an increase of 40%.

**Formula Used:** Final Price = Initial Price × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) ...

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58eda74ab609fd4f23aec04be7bb4b4c8be39ff5c94187f42a0e9a157cf74ae7.png] 

Let the **original price** be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 − 55% of 100 = 45

⇒ Price after 2nd month = 45 − 35% of 45 = 45 × 0.65 = 29.25

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 29.25 − 45% of 29.25 = 29.25 × 0.55 = 16.0875

⇒ Price after 4th month = 16.0875 + 40% of 16.0875 = 16.0875 × 1.4 = 22.5225

⇒ Total decrease from original = 100 − 22.5225 = 77.4775

⇒ Percentage decrease = (77.4775 / 100) × 100 = 77.4775%

**∴ The correct answer is 77.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%. For decreases, use negative values.

Multiplier Method

For a decrease of x%, the multiplier is (100 − x)/100. For an increase of y%, it is (100 + y)/100. Multiply all factors to get the final ratio.

Rounding Rule

When rounding to 2 decimal places, check the 3rd decimal. If it is 5 or greater, round up the 2nd decimal.

questions.question: If the height at which a ladder touches the wall is the mean proportional between 6 meters and 24 meters, at what height does the ladder touch the wall?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as √(a × b).

Given **a = 6 m** and **b = 24 m**.

Height (h) = √(6 × 24) = √144 = 12 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First value (a) = 6 m

Second value (b) = 24 m

The **height** (h) of the **ladder** on the wall is the **mean proportional**.

**Formula Used:**

If **h** is the mean proportional between **a** and **b**, then:

a : h = h : b ⇒ h² = a × b ⇒ h = √(a × b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c30e90e303980fe570fe880a38abf4277c7390c0eed9fc37a1dfe26e44123ad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ h = √(6 × 24)

⇒ h = √144

⇒ h = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional (Geometric Mean)

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is the value **x** such that a/x = x/b, which gives x = √(ab).

Third Proportional

If **a** and **b** are two numbers, then their third proportional **c** is such that a/b = b/c, which gives c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

If **a**, **b**, and **c** are three numbers, then their fourth proportional **d** is such that a/b = c/d, which gives d = (b × c)/a.

questions.question: A regular octagonal fountain has a circumradius of 10 m. Find the approximate length of each side.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **regular octagon** with **circumradius** R, the side length a is given by:

a = 2 × R × sin(180° / 8) = 2 × R × sin(22.5°)

Given: R = 10 m and sin(22.5°) ≈ 0.3827

a = 2 × 10 × 0.3827 ⇒ 20 × 0.3827

a = 7.654 m ≈ 7.65 m

**∴ The correct answer is 7.65 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Circumradius** (R) = 10 m, Number of sides (n) = 8.

Formula used: **Law of Cosines** in the triangle formed by the center and two adjacent vertices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/815c3e1248cc4527dcce815f4ec05bb4e09ea086bf1b5d090668a3f2f3ceed88.png] 

The **central angle** subtended by each side of the **regular octagon** at the center O is:

θ = 360° ÷ n ⇒ 360° ÷ 8 = 45°

In ΔOAB, let side AB = a, and OA = OB = R = 10 m.

Using **Law of Cosines**:

⇒ a² = R² + R² − 2 × R × R × cos(45°)

⇒ a² = 2R² − 2R² × (1/√2)

⇒ a² = 2R² (1 − 1/√2)

⇒ a² = 2 × 10² × (1 − 0.7071)

⇒ a² = 200 × 0.2929

⇒ a² = 58.58

⇒ a = √58.58 ≈ 7.6537 m

**∴ The correct answer is 7.65 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Regular Octagon

The area can be calculated as Area = 2(1 + √2)a², where a is the side length.

Interior and Exterior Angles

For a regular octagon, each **exterior angle** is 45° and each **interior angle** is 135°.

Inradius of a Regular Polygon

The distance from the center to the midpoint of a side is r = R × cos(180°/n).

questions.question: A bus travels at a uniform speed of 54 km/hr. How many meters does it cover in 1 minute?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **speed** from **km/hr** to **m/min** directly.

**Speed** = 54 × (1000 ÷ 60) m/min

**Speed** = 54 × (50 ÷ 3) = 18 × 50 = 900 **m/min**

In 1 **minute**, the **bus** covers 900 **meters**.

**∴ The correct answer is 900 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of the bus = 54 km/hr

**Time** taken = 1 min

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8df0d84360a6df15a152e7945040458794beecfee7acb8d389f443d28d9cb7f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1 **km** = 1000 **m** and 1 **hr** = 60 **min**

⇒ **Speed** in **m/min** = (54 × 1000) ÷ 60

⇒ **Speed** = 54000 ÷ 60 = 900 **m/min**

⇒ **Distance** = 900 **m/min** × 1 **min**

⇒ **Distance** = 900 **m**

**∴ The correct answer is 900 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Trick

To convert **speed** from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** back to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance Formula

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**. Always ensure that the units of **speed** and **time** are consistent (e.g., both in seconds or both in hours) before calculation.

Uniform Speed

When an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of **time**, it is said to be moving with **uniform speed**.

questions.question: A motorist travels a certain journey in two stages. In the first stage, he travels for one-third of the total time at 30 km/hr. In the second stage, he travels for the rest of the time at 60 km/hr. He returns to the start at a uniform speed of 75 km/hr. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **average speed** for the onward journey is the weighted average of speeds with respect to time. Onward Average Speed = (1/3 × 30) + (2/3 × 60) = 10 + 40 = 50 km/hr. Since the distance for the **onward journey** and **return journey** is equal, use the harmonic mean formula: Average Speed = (2 × Vₒₙ × Vᵣₑₜ) ÷ (Vₒₙ + Vᵣₑₜ) = (2 × 50 × 75) ÷ (50 + 75) = 7500 ÷ 125 = 60 km/hr. **∴ The correct answer is 60 km/hr.**

questions.question: The base of a triangle is 18 cm and height is 20 cm. Find the height of another triangle of double the area having base 24 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of areas: (Base₁ × Height₁) ÷ (Base₂ × Height₂) = Area₁ ÷ Area₂

Given: Area₂ = 2 × Area₁ ⇒ Area₁ : Area₂ = 1 : 2

(18 × 20) ÷ (24 × H₂) = 1 ÷ 2

360 ÷ (24 × H₂) = 1 ÷ 2

H₂ = (360 × 2) ÷ 24 = 720 ÷ 24 = 30 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base of first triangle (b₁) = 18 cm

Height of first triangle (h₁) = 20 cm

Base of second triangle (b₂) = 24 cm

Area of second triangle (A₂) = 2 × Area of first triangle (A₁)

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × **base** × **height**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09340cda05a871e6786f2a5ef9132b32b373768a88f3d392b7d815800751421b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area₁ = (1 ÷ 2) × 18 × 20

⇒ Area₁ = 9 × 20 = 180 cm²

⇒ Area₂ = 2 × Area₁ = 2 × 180 = 360 cm²

⇒ 360 = (1 ÷ 2) × 24 × h₂

⇒ 360 = 12 × h₂

⇒ h₂ = 360 ÷ 12

⇒ h₂ = 30 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

When all three sides a, b, and c are known, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c)/2.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For a triangle with all sides equal to 'a', the area is given by (√3 ÷ 4) × a².

Right-Angled Triangle

The area is (1 ÷ 2) × base × perpendicular, where the two sides forming the 90° angle act as base and height.

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 16 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern if all the taps are opened together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = Efficiency of **Tap 1** + Efficiency of **Tap 2** − Efficiency of **Tap 3**.

Since **Tap 1** fills in 4 hr and **Tap 3** empties in 4 hr, their rates cancel each other out completely.

The net filling rate is solely determined by **Tap 2**, which takes 16 hr to fill the full cistern.

Time to fill 1/4 of the cistern = 1/4 × 16 hr = 4 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time for Tap A = 4 hr, Tap B = 16 hr, and Emptying time for Tap C = 4 hr.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = L.C.M. of time taken | Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Tap Name**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency (units/hr)**
 
 

 Tap A (Fill)
 4
 16 units
 4
 
 

 Tap B (Fill)
 16
 1
 
 

 Tap C (Empty)
 4
 −4
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency when all taps are open = 4 + 1 − 4 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Required capacity to fill = 1/4 × Total Capacity = 1/4 × 16 = 4 units

⇒ Time taken = Required Capacity ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 4 units ÷ 1 unit/hr = 4 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency of Emptying Pipe

The efficiency of an **outlet** or **emptying pipe** is always taken as negative because it reduces the total volume of the **cistern**.

Net Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x hr and pipe B empties in y hr, the net part filled in 1 hr is (1/x − 1/y). If y > x, the tank will eventually fill.

Fractional Filling

To find the time for a **fractional part** of the tank, multiply the total time required for a full tank by that specific **fraction**.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the expression x³ - 3x² - 7x - k will be divisible by (x - 5).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the **Remainder Theorem**, if a polynomial is divisible by (x − 5), substituting x = 5 must yield zero.

Put **x = 5** in the expression: 5³ − 3(5²) − 7(5) − k = 0

125 − 75 − 35 − k = 0

15 − k = 0 ⇒ **k = 15**

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Polynomial P(x) = x³ − 3x² − 7x − k

Divisor = (x − 5)

**Formula Used:**

According to the **Factor Theorem**, if (x − a) is a factor of P(x), then P(a) = 0.

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the expression to be divisible by (x − 5), the remainder must be 0.

⇒ P(5) = 0

⇒ (5)³ − 3 × (5)² − 7 × (5) − k = 0

⇒ 125 − 3 × 25 − 35 − k = 0

⇒ 125 − 75 − 35 − k = 0

⇒ 50 − 35 − k = 0

⇒ 15 − k = 0

⇒ k = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remainder Theorem

When a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is always f(a).

Factor Theorem

A linear polynomial (x − a) is a factor of a polynomial f(x) if and only if f(a) = 0.

Divisibility Rule for Polynomials

If P(x) is divisible by Q(x), then every root of Q(x) must also be a root of P(x).

questions.question: If cosA = (4)/(5), find the value of (sin² A - 5cos² A + sec² A)/(tan² A) .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **cos A = 4/5**, we identify the **Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5)** where **Base = 4**, **Hypotenuse = 5**, and **Perpendicular = 3**.

Then **sin A = 3/5**, **tan A = 3/4**, and **sec A = 5/4**.

Substitute values into the expression: ((3/5)² − 5×(4/5)² + (5/4)²) ÷ (3/4)².

Numerator = (9/25 − 80/25 + 25/16) = −71/25 + 25/16 = (−1136 + 625)/400 = −511/400.

Result = (−511/400) × (16/9) = −511/(25×9) = −511/225.

**∴ The correct answer is −511/225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **cos A** = 4/5

**Formula Used:** In a right-angled triangle, **cos A = Base/Hypotenuse**. By **Pythagoras theorem**, **Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse² − Base²**. Also, **sin A = P/H**, **tan A = P/B**, and **sec A = H/B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ece245ce7dc0a0a22a8a36bc0d92fd2c6639b8c0e29d3618d03d2992b0bbc04.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Base (B)** = 4 and **Hypotenuse (H)** = 5.

⇒ **Perpendicular (P)** = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3.

⇒ **sin A** = P/H = 3/5

⇒ **tan A** = P/B = 3/4

⇒ **sec A** = H/B = 5/4

⇒ **Value** = (sin² A − 5 cos² A + sec² A) / tan² A

⇒ **Value** = ((3/5)² − 5×(4/5)² + (5/4)²) / (3/4)²

⇒ **Value** = (9/25 − 5×(16/25) + 25/16) / (9/16)

⇒ **Value** = (9/25 − 80/25 + 25/16) / (9/16) = (−71/25 + 25/16) / (9/16)

⇒ **Value** = [(−71×16 + 25×25) / (25×16)] ÷ (9/16)

⇒ **Value** = [(−1136 + 625) / 400] ÷ (9/16) = (−511/400) × (16/9)

⇒ **Value** = −511 / (25 × 9) = −511/225.

**∴ The correct answer is −511/225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard identities include sin² A + cos² A = 1, 1 + tan² A = sec² A, and 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common integer sets satisfying a² + b² = c² like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) are extremely useful in exam time-saving.

Reciprocal Ratios

The reciprocal ratios are defined as sec A = 1/cos A, cosec A = 1/sin A, and cot A = 1/tan A.

Simplify the second bracket: (2/3 + 5/14) = (28 + 15)/42 = 43/42.

Divide the results: (1/14) ÷ (43/42) = 1/14 × 42/43 = 3/43.

Simplify the final term using **BODMAS**: 1/2 ÷ (43/6) = 1/2 × 6/43 = 3/43.

Combine: 3/43 + 3/43 = 6/43.

**∴ The correct answer is 6/43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** { (15/42) ÷ (15/3) } ÷ ( (3/10) × (20/9) + (5/14) ) + (3/6) ÷ (43/20) of (20/6)

**Formula Used:** **VBODMAS** (Vinculum, Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ Step 1 (Solve Brackets): { 15/42 × 3/15 } ÷ ( 2/3 + 5/14 ) + 3/6 ÷ ( 43/20 of 20/6 )

⇒ Step 2 (Simplify Fractions): { 1/14 } ÷ ( 43/42 ) + 1/2 ÷ ( 43/20 × 20/6 )

⇒ Step 3 (Process 'Of' and Divisions): (1/14 × 42/43) + 1/2 ÷ 43/6

⇒ Step 4 (Multiplication and Reciprocal): 3/43 + (1/2 × 6/43)

⇒ Step 5 (Final Addition): 3/43 + 3/43 = 6/43

**∴ The correct answer is 6/43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

This rule defines the **precedence** of operations: Vinculum (Bar), Brackets (), Of, Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Fraction Reciprocal Rule

To divide by a **fraction**, multiply by its **reciprocal**: (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b) × (d/c).

'Of' vs Multiplication

The operator **'of'** behaves as multiplication but holds a **higher priority** than division and regular multiplication in the order of operations.

questions.question: The fourth proportional to 4, 6, and 8 is m. The third proportional to 8 and m is n. What is the value of n?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Fourth proportional** **m** = (Product of middle terms) ÷ (First term)

⇒ **m** = (6 × 8) ÷ 4 = 12

**Third proportional** **n** = (Square of second term) ÷ (First term)

⇒ **n** = (12 × 12) ÷ 8 = 144 ÷ 8 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers for **fourth proportional**: 4, 6, 8, and **m**

Numbers for **third proportional**: 8, **m**, and **n**

**Formula Used:**

1. If a, b, c, d are in **proportion**, then a/b = c/d

2. If a, b, c are in **continued proportion**, then a/b = b/c (where c is the **third proportional**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7842d763e45557fdc2f3e07a80aab53822432178c930f34351fa64f3c4ffdaa8.png] 

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Finding **m**

⇒ 4 ÷ 6 = 8 ÷ **m**

⇒ 4 × **m** = 6 × 8

⇒ 4 × **m** = 48

⇒ **m** = 12

Step 2: Finding **n**

⇒ 8 ÷ 12 = 12 ÷ **n**

⇒ 8 × **n** = 12 × 12

⇒ 8 × **n** = 144

⇒ **n** = 144 ÷ 8 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

For four numbers a, b, c, and d to be in proportion, the relation is a/b = c/d, which gives d = (b × c) / a.

Third Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c to be in continued proportion, the relation is a/b = b/c, which gives c = b² / a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by the formula √(a × b).

questions.question: The H.C.F. and L.C.M. of two numbers are 25 and 500, respectively. If the first number is divided by 2, the quotient is 50 and the remainder is zero. Find the second number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**First Number** = 2 × 50 = 100.

Product of numbers = **HCF** × **LCM**.

100 × **Second Number** = 25 × 500.

**Second Number** = 12500 ÷ 100 = 125.

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**H.C.F.** = 25

**L.C.M.** = 500

**First number** when divided by 2 gives **quotient** = 50 and **remainder** = 0.

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend** = (**Divisor** × **Quotient**) + **Remainder**

**Product of two numbers** = **H.C.F.** × **L.C.M.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00cf9343d4e21482363dd963d55e0f0caa7fe135f60247d6dae0f56785e2ecb1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **First number** (N₁) = (2 × 50) + 0

⇒ N₁ = 100

⇒ N₁ × N₂ = 25 × 500

⇒ 100 × N₂ = 12500

⇒ N₂ = 12500 ÷ 100

⇒ N₂ = 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule

For any two numbers a and b, the relationship is: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the greatest number that divides each of the two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** of two or more numbers is the smallest number (not zero) that is a multiple of all the numbers.

Division Algorithm

The rule states that **Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**, where 0 ≤ Remainder < Divisor.

questions.question: Five friends participated in a cooking contest and scored 6, 8, 7, 9, and 5 out of 10, respectively. What is the arithmetic mean of their scores?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base average** of 7.

Calculate **deviations** from 7: (6−7), (8−7), (7−7), (9−7), (5−7) ⇒ −1, +1, 0, +2, −2.

**Net deviation** = −1 + 1 + 0 + 2 − 2 = 0.

Required **Mean** = Base Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Count) = 7 + (0 ÷ 5) = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scores of five friends: 6, 8, 7, 9, and 5.

Total number of friends (n) = 5.

**Formula Used:**

**Arithmetic Mean** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6004ee3460e7e51c9fd1269448822394badcf06201032de6d2059b81087820b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of scores = 6 + 8 + 7 + 9 + 5

⇒ Sum of scores = 35

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 35 ÷ 5

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Arithmetic Mean

When observations have different levels of importance, the mean is calculated as Σ(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ, where w is the weight.

Properties of Mean

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Median vs Mean

While the mean is the **average**, the **median** is the middle value of a sorted data set. For the set (5, 6, 7, 8, 9), the median is also 7.

questions.question: Evaluate 22³ + (-15)³ + (-7)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of three numbers **a + b + c = 0**, then **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**.

Check the sum of given numbers: 22 + (−15) + (−7) = 22 − 22 = 0.

Apply the trick: 3 × 22 × (−15) × (−7).

Calculation: 66 × 105 = 6930.

**∴ The correct answer is 6930.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: **22³ + (−15)³ + (−7)³**

Let **a = 22**, **b = −15**, and **c = −7**.

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the sum (a + b + c):

⇒ a + b + c = 22 + (−15) + (−7)

⇒ a + b + c = 22 − 15 − 7 = 0

⇒ Since **a + b + c = 0**, the identity simplifies to: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ Substituting the values: 3 × 22 × (−15) × (−7)

⇒ = 3 × 22 × 105

⇒ = 66 × 105

⇒ = 66 × (100 + 5) = 6600 + 330 = 6930

**∴ The correct answer is 6930.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The Cubic Identity

The expression a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc is always zero if a + b + c = 0 or if a = b = c.

Square of Trinomial

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). This is used to find individual squares or sum of products.

Difference of Cubes

x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²), useful for factoring two-term cubic expressions.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 4 : 3 : 13, and their LCM is 4524. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **ratio** of three numbers is a : b : c and their **LCM** is given, then **HCF** = LCM ÷ LCM(a, b, c).

LCM of ratio parts (4, 3, 13) = 4 × 3 × 13 = 156 (since they are **co-prime**).

HCF = 4524 ÷ 156 = 29.

**∴ The correct answer is 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of three numbers = 4 : 3 : 13

**LCM** of these numbers = 4524

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b44b489086ab4749f05649e38483569db12e10fc4e598b2d1741e74a6faf811a.png] 

Let the **HCF** of the three numbers be x.

The three numbers can be represented as 4x, 3x, and 13x.

The **LCM** of (4x, 3x, 13x) is calculated as:

⇒ LCM = x × LCM(4, 3, 13)

Since 4, 3, and 13 have no common factors other than 1 (they are **pairwise co-prime**):

⇒ LCM(4, 3, 13) = 4 × 3 × 13 = 156

Now, equating to the given LCM value:

⇒ 156x = 4524

⇒ x = 4524 ÷ 156

⇒ x = 29

The **HCF** of the three numbers is x = 29.

**∴ The correct answer is 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF × LCM.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of (a/b, c/d, e/f) = HCF(a, c, e) ÷ LCM(b, d, f).

Co-prime Numbers

Two or more numbers are called **co-prime** if their **HCF** is 1. The LCM of a set of co-prime numbers is simply their product.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of (a/b, c/d, e/f) = LCM(a, c, e) ÷ HCF(b, d, f).

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks a jacket at ₹2,000. He gives a 20% discount, but charges 5% GST on the discounted price. What is the final price the customer pays?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier = (**1 − 0.20**) × (**1 + 0.05**) = 0.8 × 1.05 = 0.84

Final Price = **Marked Price** × 0.84

Final Price = 2000 × 0.84 = 1680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹2,000

**Discount** = 20%

**GST** = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3ea694ff3593daa9dde21bc3a8fbaf3521c849fe8c00c4c147d6e7491ebfd21.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Discount** = 20% of 2000 = (20/100) × 2000 = 400

⇒ **Price after Discount** = 2000 − 400 = 1600

⇒ **GST** = 5% of 1600 = (5/100) × 1600 = 80

⇒ **Final Price** = 1600 + 80 = 1680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Percentage Change

When a value is changed successively by x% and y%, the net effective change is (x + y + (xy/100))%. Note that a discount is a negative change.

Marked Price (MP)

Present ratio (**Amit** : **Sumit**) = 2 : 1 | Ratio 5 years ago = 5 : 2.

Equate the age difference (2−1=1 and 5−2=3) by multiplying the present ratio by 3.

New Present ratio = 6 : 3 | Ratio 5 years ago = 5 : 2.

Difference in ratio parts (6−5 or 3−2) = 1 unit.

1 unit = 5 years. Therefore, **Sumit** present age = 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Present age of **Amit** is twice that of **Sumit**.

⇒ 4x − 10 = 5x − 25

⇒ x = 15

questions.question: The Punchhi Commission (2007) was primarily constituted to examine and make recommendations regarding which provision of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centre-State Relations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Punchhi Commission** was established by the **Government of India** on **27th April 2007** to re-examine the evolving nature of **Centre-State Relations** in the context of globalized economic and political shifts.
 
• The commission was chaired by **Madan Mohan Punchhi**, the former **Chief Justice of India**, and included other prominent members such as **Dhirendra Singh**, **Vinod Kumar Duggal**, and **N.R. Madhava Menon**.
 
• Its primary objective was to review the existing arrangements between the Union and the States, building upon the foundational work done by the **Sarkaria Commission** in the 1980s.
 
• The commission addressed critical issues including **internal security**, **communal violence**, the devolution of powers to **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, and the fiscal responsibilities of the states.
 
• It provided specific recommendations on the exercise of discretionary powers by the **Governor** and the implementation of **Article 355** and **Article 356** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Report and Recommendations:**

 
 
• The commission submitted its comprehensive report in **seven volumes** to the Union government on **31st March 2010**.
 
• One major recommendation was that the **Governor** should be an eminent person from outside the state and should not have participated in active politics for at least a few years prior to the appointment.
 
• It suggested that **Article 356** (President's Rule) should be used only as a last resort, following the principles established in the **S.R. Bommai case (1994)**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):** Contained in **Part IV** (Articles 36 to 51) of the Constitution, these are non-justiciable guidelines for the government to ensure social and economic justice.
 
• **Fundamental Rights:** Listed in **Part III** (Articles 12 to 35), these are justiciable rights guaranteed to citizens, protecting individual liberties against state encroachment.
 
• **Electoral Reforms:** This domain is typically covered by committees like the **Dinesh Goswami Committee** (1990) and the **Indrajit Gupta Committee** (1998) rather than the Punchhi Commission.

questions.question: The Vinaya Pitaka, one of the principal Buddhist texts, mainly focuses on which of the following?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vinaya Pitaka** is the first of the three divisions of the **Tripitaka** (the 'Three Baskets'), which forms the primary canon of **Theravada Buddhism**.
 
• Its primary function is to govern the **monastic order** by providing a comprehensive framework of **rules and regulations** for the **Sangha**.
 
• The text details the **ethical conduct** and discipline required for **bhikkhus** (monks) and **bhikkhunis** (nuns), covering aspects such as robes, food, residence, and social interactions.
 
• It contains the **Patimokkha**, which is a collection of 227 rules for monks and 311 for nuns, intended to be recited during the **Uposatha** (fortnightly assembly).
 
• The **Vinaya Pitaka** is categorized into three main sections: the **Suttavibhanga** (analysis of rules), the **Khandhaka** (procedural rules and life of the Buddha), and the **Parivara** (a summary and analytical manual).
 
• It was traditionally compiled during the **First Buddhist Council** held at **Rajgir** (Rajagriha) under the leadership of **Mahakasyapa**, shortly after the death of **Gautama Buddha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Sutta Pitaka**:

 
 
• Consists of over 10,000 **sutras** or discourses delivered by the Buddha to diverse audiences.
 
• It includes the **Jataka Tales**, which are popular narratives describing the **previous lives** of the Buddha in both human and animal forms.
 
• It is divided into five collections known as **Nikayas**: Digha, Majjhima, Samyutta, Anguttara, and Khuddaka.
 
 
 
• **The Abhidhamma Pitaka**:
 
 
• Focuses on the **philosophical, psychological, and systematic** analysis of the Buddha's teachings rather than simple moral stories.
 
• It explores complex themes related to **cosmology**, ethics, and the nature of mind and matter.
 
 
 
• **Language and Origin**:
 
 
• The **Tripitaka** was originally preserved through oral tradition and later written down in **Pali** in Sri Lanka during the 1st century BCE.
 
• The term **Pitaka** literally means 'basket', signifying the containers in which the original **palm-leaf manuscripts** were kept.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor strengthened imperial authority by introducing the **Mansabdari system** and a **centralized bureaucracy**?

The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was the administrative bedrock of the **Mughal Empire**, formally introduced and structured by **Akbar** around **1571** to streamline both military and civil services.
 
• Under this system, the term **Mansab** designated a rank or position, which determined the status, salary, and military responsibilities of an official within the **centralized bureaucracy**.
 
• The rank was divided into two distinct designations: **Zat**, which indicated the personal status and fixed the salary of the **Mansabdar**, and **Sawar**, which specified the number of cavalrymen and horses the officer was required to maintain for the state.
 
• **Akbar** used this system to bypass the traditional influence of hereditary tribal chieftains and powerful ethnic factions, ensuring that all officials were directly accountable to the **Emperor** for their appointments and promotions.
 
• Remuneration for **Mansabdars** was provided either in cash (known as **Naqdi**) or through the assignment of land revenue from specific territories called **Jagirs**, though these lands were non-hereditary and subject to frequent transfer to prevent local power bases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shah Jahan**

 
 
• He reigned during the **Golden Age** of Mughal architecture and introduced the **Mahana** (month-scale) system to address the disparity between the estimated revenue (**Jama**) and the actual revenue collected (**Hasil**).
 
 
 
• **Humayun**
 
 
• As the second **Mughal Emperor** and father of **Akbar**, his reign was characterized by internal struggle and his eventual expulsion by **Sher Shah Suri**; he did not establish a formalized administrative system like the **Mansabdari**.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Shah**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Rangila**, his rule in the **18th century** saw the rapid disintegration of the centralized authority and the eventual collapse of the **Mansabdari** and **Jagirdari** systems due to administrative corruption and external invasions.

• **Open Market Operations (OMOs)** are the primary quantitative tools used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to regulate the **money supply** and liquidity within the economy.
 
• The process involves the simultaneous buying and selling of **Government Securities (G-Secs)** and **Treasury Bills** by the central bank in the open market.
 
• When the **RBI** determines that there is excess **liquidity** leading to **inflationary pressures**, it sells securities to the public and commercial banks, effectively absorbing cash from the system.
 
• In scenarios where the economy requires a boost in **liquidity** (monetary expansion), the **RBI** purchases securities, thereby injecting **cash** into the banking channels.
 
• These operations are conducted under the framework of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, and are aimed at managing **interest rates** and maintaining **price stability**.

questions.question: When considering the dimensions of electric charge, which fundamental units must be combined to express it in terms of SI base quantities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**current and time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric charge** is a fundamental physical property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field. In the **International System of Units (SI)**, charge is treated as a **derived quantity**.
 
• The definition of **Electric Current (I)** is the rate at which **electric charge (Q)** flows through a cross-section of a conductor. Mathematically, this is expressed by the equation **Q = I × t**, where **t** represents **time**.
 
• The **SI base units** for current and time are the **Ampere (A)** and the **Second (s)**, respectively. Since charge is the product of these two, its units must be expressed as the combination of **current** and **time**.
 
• Through **dimensional analysis**, the dimensions of electric charge are represented as **[M⁰ L⁰ T¹ A¹]**. Here, **A** stands for the dimension of **electric current** and **T** stands for the dimension of **time**.
 
• The specific derived unit for electric charge is the **Coulomb (C)**. One Coulomb is equivalent to the amount of charge transferred by a steady current of one **Ampere** in one **second** (1 C = 1 A × s).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SI Base Quantities**:

 
 
• The **General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)** has established seven base quantities: **Length** (meter), **Mass** (kilogram), **Time** (second), **Electric Current** (ampere), **Thermodynamic Temperature** (kelvin), **Amount of Substance** (mole), and **Luminous Intensity** (candela).
 
• While charge is often thought of as more "fundamental" in physics theory, the **Ampere** was historically chosen as the base unit because it can be defined and measured more accurately through the mechanical force between current-carrying wires.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Electric Charge**:
 
 
• Charge is **quantized**, meaning it exists in discrete packets. The **elementary charge (e)** is approximately 1.602 × 10−¹⁹ Coulombs.
 
• Charge is **conserved**; it can neither be created nor destroyed in an isolated system, only transferred from one body to another.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity**, possessing only magnitude and no direction, unlike current density or electric field vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following natural regions is dominated by xerophytic or drought-resisting scrub with long roots, few or no leaves, and waxy or needle-shaped foliage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hot desert (Sahara type) region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The vegetation in **Hot Deserts**, such as the **Sahara**, **Thar**, and **Arabian** deserts, consists primarily of **xerophytic** or drought-resistant scrub. These plants are specifically adapted to survive in environments with **extreme aridity** and high **evapotranspiration**.
 
• A primary adaptation is the development of **long taproots** that extend deep into the soil to reach the **groundwater table** or permanent **aquifers**, ensuring a steady water supply during long dry spells.
 
• To minimize water loss through **transpiration**, these plants have evolved **needle-shaped**, **waxy**, or **leathery** foliage. In many species, leaves are absent or modified into **spines** and **thorns** to protect stored moisture from herbivores.
 
• Many desert plants are **succulents**, possessing thick, fleshy stems or leaves capable of storing large quantities of water. The **photosynthetic** process often occurs in the green stems rather than the leaves to further conserve moisture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In the architecture of the Windows Operating System, which crucial component acts as the bridge between the application programs and the core hardware, operating in a protected mode to manage process scheduling, memory allocation, and interrupt handling?

options.text: Kernel, which contains the executive services, process manager, and security reference monitor.
Windows Shell (Explorer), which manages the desktop, taskbar, and file system user interface.
Win32 Subsystem, which translates instructions for 32-bit applications and manages display output.
Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL), which isolates the kernel from platform-specific hardware differences.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kernel, which contains the executive services, process manager, and security reference monitor.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kernel** is the central component of the **Windows NT architecture**, operating in **Kernel Mode** (Protected Mode) to ensure system stability by preventing user applications from directly accessing critical hardware.
 
• It serves as the essential bridge between **Application Software** and the **Physical Hardware**, managing the execution of threads and handling **Hardware Interrupts** or exceptions.
 
• The **Executive Services** layer within the kernel contains specialized components like the **Memory Manager**, which handles **Virtual Memory** and physical memory allocation, and the **Process Manager**, which governs the life cycle of system processes.
 
• The **Security Reference Monitor (SRM)** is a vital kernel component that enforces **Access Control Lists (ACLs)** and manages security auditing, ensuring that only authorized processes can access specific system resources.
 
• Through **Thread Scheduling**, the kernel determines which execution thread receives **CPU time**, optimizing performance across **Multiprocessor** systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Windows Shell (Explorer)**

 
 
• Operates primarily in **User Mode** rather than protected kernel mode.
 
• Responsible for the **Graphical User Interface (GUI)**, including the **Taskbar**, Start Menu, and file management via **explorer.exe**.
 
 
 
• **Win32 Subsystem**
 
 
• Functions as an **Environment Subsystem** that provides the primary **Application Programming Interface (API)** for Windows programs.
 
• Manages **Display Output**, keyboard/mouse input, and console windows through **csrss.exe** and **win32k.sys**.
 
 
 
• **Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL)**
 
 
• A low-level **Kernel-mode** library (hal.dll) that sits between the kernel and the hardware.
 
• Its primary purpose is to hide **Platform-Specific** hardware differences (like different motherboards or chipsets) from the operating system, making Windows **Portable** across different hardware architectures.

questions.question: The conversion of chemical energy into electrical energy and then into light and thermal energy occurs in which of the following cases?

options.text: When a flashlight is turned on

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a flashlight is turned on**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **flashlight**, the sequence of energy transformation begins in the **battery** (or dry cell), which acts as a reservoir of **chemical energy** stored within its electrodes and electrolytes.
 
• When the switch is moved to the **ON** position, it completes the **electrical circuit**, triggering a **chemical reaction** (typically a redox reaction) that releases electrons, thereby converting **chemical energy** into **electrical energy**.
 
• This **electric current** then flows through the **conductors** to the **light source**, which can be an **incandescent bulb** or an **LED** (Light Emitting Diode).
 
• Inside an incandescent bulb, the **tungsten filament** offers resistance to the flow of electrons, heating up significantly (**Joule heating**) until it glows, which converts the **electrical energy** into both **light energy** (photons) and **thermal energy** (heat).
 
• In the case of an **LED**, while the conversion to **light** is more efficient through **electroluminescence**, a small amount of **thermal energy** is still generated as a byproduct of the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy Transformations in Other Cases:**

 
 
• **When a candle burns**: The **chemical energy** stored in the wax is converted directly into **light** and **thermal energy** via **combustion**, without an intermediate electrical phase.
 
• **When a fan rotates**: The **electrical energy** supplied from the mains or a battery is converted primarily into **mechanical energy** (specifically **kinetic energy**) using an **electric motor** and **electromagnetic induction**.
 
• **When water is boiled**: If an electric kettle is used, **electrical energy** is converted into **thermal energy** through **resistive heating**; if a gas stove is used, **chemical energy** is converted directly into **thermal energy**.
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy**: These processes are governed by the principle that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one state to another.

• In the majority of **dicotyledonous plants**, the direct elongation of the **radicle** leads to the formation of the **primary root** which grows inside the soil.
 
• The **primary root** is the main central axis that persists throughout the life of the plant and gives rise to lateral branches of various orders, such as **secondary roots** and **tertiary roots**.
 
• The combination of the **primary root** and its lateral branches is defined as the **tap root system**, which is a characteristic feature of **Dicots**.
 
• This system is adapted for deep penetration into the soil to ensure better anchorage and efficient absorption of water and minerals from deeper layers.
 
• A classic example of the **tap root system** is seen in the **Mustard plant** (Brassica campestris), as well as in **Mango**, **Pea**, and **Gram**.

• These are roots that develop from any part of the plant other than the **radicle**, such as the stem or leaves.
 
• Examples include roots found in **Grass**, **Monstera**, and the **Banyan tree**.
 
 
 
• **Prop root system**:
 
 
• A specialized type of **adventitious root** primarily designed for mechanical support.
 
• They arise from heavy horizontal branches and grow vertically downward into the soil, acting as pillars, famously seen in the **Banyan tree** (Ficus benghalensis).

questions.question: In semi-arid north-western India, intensified canal irrigation leads to rising soil salinity and falling crop yields. What best explains this, and what correction is required?

options.text: Prolonged irrigation causes waterlogging; priority is shifting to drought-resistant crop varieties.
Excess irrigation washes nutrients downward; priority is increasing chemical fertiliser use.
Raised water table causes salt rise; priority is drainage improvement and salt leaching.
Cold canal water stresses crops physiologically; priority is regulating irrigation water temperature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raised water table causes salt rise; priority is drainage improvement and salt leaching**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **semi-arid regions** of **North-Western India**, specifically in states like **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Rajasthan**, the introduction of intensive **canal irrigation** without adequate drainage systems has led to a phenomenon known as **waterlogging**.
 
• Excessive seepage from unlined canals and over-irrigation causes the **groundwater table** to rise steadily over time, eventually reaching the **capillary fringe** near the soil surface.
 
• Through **capillary action**, water carrying dissolved minerals and salts (such as **sodium**, **magnesium**, and **calcium**) is pulled upward; when this water evaporates due to high temperatures, the salts are left behind, forming a saline crust or **efflorescence**.
 
• This process, known as **soil salinization**, increases the **osmotic pressure** of the soil solution, making it difficult for crops to extract water and nutrients, thereby severely reducing **crop yields**.
 
• The most effective corrective measures involve installing **sub-surface drainage** to lower the water table and practicing **leaching**, where excess fresh water is applied to dissolve and wash the salts deep into the ground, away from the **root zone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi Canal Project (IGNP)**:

 
 
• While it transformed the **Thar Desert** into a green belt, it also caused massive **ecological imbalances** due to rising salinity in districts like **Ganganagar** and **Hanumangarh**.
 
 
 
• **Soil Terms**:
 
 
• Saline soils are often locally referred to as **Reh**, **Usar**, or **Kallar** in Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Remedial Strategies**:
 
 
• **Drought-resistant crops** are designed for water scarcity, not for soils with high **salinity** or **alkalinity**.
 
• Adding **chemical fertilizers** to saline soil can worsen the chemical imbalance and soil structure without addressing the physical presence of salts.
 
• **Gypsum application** is specifically used for **sodic (alkaline) soils** to replace sodium with calcium, but it must be accompanied by proper drainage.

questions.question: Public Interest Litigation is an example of which doctrine?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Public Interest Litigation (PIL)** is a powerful tool used by the Indian judiciary to protect the legal rights of the general public and marginalized communities. It is considered the most significant manifestation of **Judicial Activism** in India, as it allows the courts to take a proactive role in social justice and administrative oversight.
 
• The concept of **Judicial Activism** refers to a philosophy where judges go beyond traditional interpretations of the law to protect individual rights and ensure social welfare, often stepping in when the **Legislature** or **Executive** fails to act.
 
• The most distinctive feature of **PIL** is the relaxation of the traditional rule of **Locus Standi**. Under this relaxed doctrine, any public-spirited individual or organization can approach the court on behalf of those who are unable to do so due to poverty, ignorance, or social disability.
 
• The foundations of **PIL** were laid in the late **1970s** and early **1980s** by eminent jurists such as **Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer** and **Justice P.N. Bhagwati**. In the landmark case of **S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India (1981)**, the **Supreme Court** formally established the legitimacy of **PIL**.
 
• **PIL** can be filed in the **Supreme Court** under **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** and in various **High Courts** under **Article 226**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• While **PIL** utilizes the power of **Judicial Review**, it specifically represents the activist spirit of the court to initiate justice for the masses.
 
 
 
• **Executive Action**:
 
 
• Refers to the administrative functions and decisions made by the **Government** and its officials.
 
• **PIL** often acts as a check on arbitrary or illegal **Executive Action** to ensure accountability.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Neutrality**:
 
 
• The principle that judges should remain objective and impartial, making decisions strictly based on the letter of the law without being influenced by social or political pressures.
 
• **Judicial Activism** is often viewed as the opposite of **Judicial Restraint** or strict neutrality, as it involves active court intervention in policy matters.
 
 
 
• **Epistolary Jurisdiction**:
 
 
• A unique aspect of **PIL** where the court treats simple letters or postcards addressed to the judges as formal writ petitions to address grievances of the poor.
